track.title: Chahargah
track.notes: Tagged title: Chahrgah. Same performance as 'The Masters of Persian Traditional Music, Sehtar' (1991) track 2; that transfer runs 0.60% slower (onset alignment), about 10 cents lower if the speed carries the pitch.

just_intervals.note: measured octave minus 1200 ¢, register to register

progression.narrative: The performance opens on B3 and dwells most on B in Phrase 1. Phrase 3 (0:25.8) introduces E, Gb, Gs, Bb, centred on B. Phrase 4 (0:38.7) introduces Eb, centred on B. Phrase 6 (1:05.2) introduces Cs, centred on B. The line peaks at Cs5 (522.1 Hz) at 2:25.4. It closes on the tonic (Gs4 → Gb4 → Eb4 → Cs4 → B2 → B2).

theory_fit.name: Pythagorean / Safi al-Din
theory_fit.description: Nearest note of the 17-note gamut generated by pure fifths (±8) from the tonic.

theory_fit.name: Farhat interval classes
theory_fit.description: Interval classes Hormoz Farhat measured in performance practice ("The Dastgah Concept in Persian Music", 1990). Approximate centres.

flags: tonic B set in the catalog (Chahargah's finalis, about Bb +30 cents (237.2 Hz): the pitch set fits Chahargah exactly from it (7 of 7 degrees, nothing extra), and the other transfer of this performance (Masters, 1991) voted that note. The vote picked the 3rd below, Chahargah's usual opening note (Farhat 1990, p. 56). Inference, not yet by ear); the runs' vote favoured 383.4 Hz (G)

tonic cross-checks disagree in E1-whole-mono-eb3f3c51296d, E1-whole-mono-198708ffe184: Tonic 238.8 Hz (A#3) via temporal-cadence. cadence agrees (119.5 Hz). drone picked 356.5 Hz (F4), a fourth away — likely the dominant; resolved to the tonic. marginalized agrees (238.8 Hz).
